categories.description: Proximates are nutrients that contribute energy to a food or beverage.
Group of organic compounds containing the carboxylic group -C(O)OH, formed by the oxidation of aldehydes. Generally analysed by chromotography.

Minerals are inorganic substances needed in the diet in small amounts to help regulate body function. From around the mid 1990's onwards, most mineral levels have been determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) or inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). Before that time, atomic absorption spectroscopy was used for most mineral determination unless noted otherwise. The more recent techniques are more sensitive and therefore likely to be more reliable for minerals present in low levels.
Vitamins are organic compounds that are needed in the diet in small amounts.

Fatty acids are classified as saturated, polyunsaturated or monounsaturated depending on the presence or absence of double bonds on the carbon molecules. Saturated fatty acids contain no double bond, monounsaturated fatty acids contain one double bond per molecule, and polyunsaturated fatty acids contain more than one double bond per molecule. Polyunsaturated fatty acids can be further subdivided into those that are omega - 6 fatty acids and those that are omega - 3 fatty acids. Although all fatty acid values reported have been generated using chromatographic methods the more recent data are considered more reliable as newer techniques are better able to separate closely related fatty acids, particularly where these occur in very low levels. Fatty acids have been measured as a percentage of all extracted fatty acids and this has been converted to a mass of fatty acids using the measured fat content of the food and a conversion factor (Greenfield and Southgate, 2003: Mooney et al., 2002: Nichols, Virtue et al., 1998: Nichols, Mooney et al., 1998: Nichols et al., 2002)

Dietary amino acids are classified as essential or non-essential. Essential amino acids cannot be manufactured by the body and must be supplied in the diet. The non-essential amino acids are also essential for health, but can be synthesized in the body from the essential amino acids. Tryptophan, an essential amino acid was determined using a separate HPLC procedure or a colorimetric procedure.

200.description:
Search the Australian Food Composition Database (AFCD Release 3.0, Food Standards Australia New Zealand) for foods by name (GET https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/food-nutrient-databases/afcd/search/api/foods/alphabetical, the complete catalogue of 1,588 foods, or /foods/alphabetical/{letter} when `letter` is given). AFCD has no server-side search: the program applies `query` as a case-insensitive substring match over the food name and its `inclusions` (alternative names), exactly as the AFCD site does, then filters by food group / sub food group and pages the result. Each row carries the Public Food Key (pfk) for get_food, the AUSNUT classification code, the food group pair and the public food page URL. Returns an empty `foods` list for a query nothing matches; `not_found` for a food_group_id / sub_food_group_id that does not exist in AFCD or a page past the last one.
